en: Cūḷaniddesa:
Verses of the Pārāyaṇa Chapter 4.
Verses in Praise of the Pārāyaṇa.
“I shall sing the Pārāyana,” said the Venerable Piṅgiya,
“just as you have seen, so you have declared.”
Vimala, Bhūrimedhasa,
Nikkāma, Nibbāna, and Nāga—
what reason could they have to speak falsely?
For one who has abandoned the stains of delusion,
who has cast off conceit and hypocrisy—
come, I shall now proclaim his praise.
The Buddha, the dispeller of darkness, the all-seeing,
who has reached the end of the world and transcended all states of existence, [speaks] speech endowed with beauty.
The one free from taints, who has abandoned all suffering,
whose name is Truth— the Brahmā— has been attended by me.
Just as a bird leaves behind a small thicket, so have I left behind the world.
One might dwell in a forest abounding in fruit;
even so have I, having abandoned those who see little,
reached the great ocean like a swan.
Before the teaching of Gotama, they used to prophesy:
"It was thus," and "It will be so."
All that is merely "thus it has been said";
all that is merely an increase of logic.
One who dispels darkness remains serene.
He is possessed of splendor, the maker of light;
Gotama is of vast wisdom,
Gotama is of vast intelligence.
He who taught me the Dhamma—
visible here and now, timeless,
the destruction of craving, free from affliction—
“For whom there is no likeness anywhere.
“Why indeed do you dwell apart from him,
even for a moment, O Piṅgiya?”
O Gotamas of vast wisdom,
O Gotamas of great intelligence!
He who taught the Dhamma to you—
Visible here and now, timeless,
the destruction of craving, free from peril—
of which there is no likeness anywhere.
“I do not dwell apart from them even for a moment, O brahmin;
the Gotamas possess abundant wisdom.”
The Gotamas of vast wisdom,
who taught me the Dhamma that is visible here and now and timeless.
I see with my mind as if with an eye him who has destroyed craving, who is free from calamity, and for whom there is no comparison anywhere.
Day and night, O Brahmin, being diligent,
I pass the night paying homage;
by that alone, I consider myself never separated [from the Buddha].
Faith, rapture, mind, and mindfulness—
these do not depart from the teaching of Gotama;
in whichever direction the one of vast wisdom goes, [they follow].
I was led away by that very same [fate].
For me, now old and with failing strength,
my body does not go there by itself.
I go constantly according to my intention,
for my mind, O Brahmin, is bound to it;
lying in the mud, I am quivering.
Island seeking an island,
I then beheld the Fully Awakened One,
who has crossed the flood and is free from taints.
“As Vakkali was released in faith,
as were Bhadrāvudha and Āḷavika Gotama,
even so you too shall release your faith.”
“You too, Piṅgiya, shall go to the further shore of the realm of death.
“Having heard the words of the Sage, I have gained even greater confidence;”
The Perfectly Awakened One, who has removed the veil [of ignorance],
is free from harshness and possesses inspired eloquence;
having directly known the higher deities, he—
He knows all things, both high and low;
the Teacher who brings an end to questions for those who declare themselves full of doubt.
Unshakable and unassailable,
for whom there is no comparison anywhere;
I shall certainly go [to that state], of this I have no doubt.
“Thus, remember me as one whose mind is resolutely intent.
The verses of the *Pārāyanānugīti* are concluded.
